brief.headline: Indian Markets Face Crude Pressures as IT Stocks Navigate Rupee Appreciation Risks
brief.summary: Indian markets open under pressure as Brent crude nears $95 per barrel and the rupee falls to 92.40 against the US dollar. Global sentiment remains mixed as central banks globally lean hawkish amid persistent inflation risks.

takeaways.text: Adani Enterprises and Adani Power plan public bond sales to raise at least Rs 20 billion, reviving India's public debt issuance.
The NSE received RBI approval to launch corporate bond index futures, enabling better portfolio hedging for market participants.
Jefferies warns that rupee recovery spells 2-4 percent EPS cuts for large Indian IT firms.
Siemens Energy India reported an 81.5 percent Y-o-Y rise in September quarter PAT to Rs 653 crore, driving shares higher.
Nvidia halted chip shipments to Southeast Asia as US export controls step up to prevent Chinese access to AI computing power.
WhatsApp is partnering with Jio to launch an international data eSIM feature in India.

sections.india: Indian government bonds fell as Brent crude topped $95 per barrel, with the Reserve Bank of India flagging continued food inflation risks. The rupee dropped 20 paise to 92.40 against the US dollar in early trade amid higher crude prices and US tariff proposals. Meanwhile, corporate updates saw Siemens Energy post an 81.5% Y-o-Y net profit jump, while BSE shares hit a 4-month high following an HDFC Securities upgrade to 'Buy'.
sections.world: European stocks closed higher on easing tariff fears and ECB leadership continuity, with Pablo Hernandez de Cos slated for the ECB presidency. US markets faced ongoing inflation concerns as hawkish Federal Reserve signals kept rate-hike expectations alive despite tech-led volatility. Oil climbed as attacks on a Saudi refinery threatened regional crude exports.
sections.tech: Nvidia halted chip shipments to Southeast Asia to comply with stricter US export controls preventing Chinese access to advanced AI computing power. The S&P considered a credit downgrade for Nvidia over governance and key-man risks. In India, WhatsApp partnered with Jio to launch an international data eSIM feature.

stories.summary: A CBS News investigation has found that Nvidia is selling its most advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips to at least two US-based companies controlled by Chinese-owned firms, raising questions over the effectiveness of US export controls aimed at keeping sensitive technology away from China.

stories.title: ChatGPT users may hit limits faster as OpenAI combines Chat and Work, but Instant remains unlimited
stories.summary: OpenAI is merging ChatGPT's Chat and Work features under a single usage limit, with a wider rollout planned for December 2026. While Instant model access will remain unlimited, the company's heaviest users may hit advanced model usage limits sooner, sparking concerns among Pro subscribers.

stories.title: Anthropic chief Dario Amodei denies wanting humans to 'surrender' free will to AI
stories.summary: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei on Wednesday denied wanting humanity to give up its free will to AI, calling it "absurd" to attribute the idea to him as rival tech leaders push back. "No, I do not believe that we should 'surrender human free will' to AI systems, and it's absurd to suggest that I do," Amodei wrote in a lengthy post on X, a week after Anthropic's record-setting stock market debut.

stories.title: Greaves Electric targets 2x sales volume for Ampere escooter in FY27
